payload.title: Each arbiter arm recognises a held group inside its mint loop, which a discretionary admission refusal ends with a break, so the held groups behind the refusal are neither named in skipped nor counted in the once-per-claim governance disclosure, and the disclosed held_count and id list depend on where the break fell.
evidence: aria-kernel/aria_kernel/judge_fanout.py:1001-1022 (split arm: held is filled inside the loop, an admission refusal at 1018-1022 breaks out)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/judge_fanout.py:1053 (the disclosure runs after the loop over whatever was visited)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/judge_fanout.py:1272-1295 (anchor arm: the same inline hold branch and the same break)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/judge_fanout.py:730-747 (_disclose_tree_holds: the claim is tool, reason, held_count and the first 20 ids of the visited held groups)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/tool_registry.py:786-792 (append_tools_governance_once dedups by claim, so each distinct held_count writes its own row)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/judge_fanout.py:1057-1064 (_arbiter_admission: the door is discretionary: a refusal is a normal outcome that holds for the rest of the cycle, so the arm stops asking)
payload.rule_violated: A standing fact is disclosed whole or not at all (the reason the hold is disclosed once per claim on governance, ARIA-MEDIUM-644); a count that depends on the iteration order and on the admission door is a measurement that is wrong.
payload.notes: 40 groups are held; sorted by key, the third group needs an arbiter and the door refuses it: the arm breaks, so held_count is 2 and only those two ids are disclosed, and the 38 held groups behind the refusal appear nowhere. The next night the door is open, the claim changes to held_count 40 and writes another row, and a night of refusal at a different group writes a third. The held share read from these rows (M5, M6) undercounts exactly when the pipeline is under pressure, and the two copies of the branch must be kept in step by hand. Close condition: Classify held groups before the mint loop with one shared helper used by both arms (hold detection no longer inside the loop), disclose all of them, and pin with a test that an admission refusal on the first non-held group still names every held group in skipped and in one disclosure with the full held_count. Verified at origin/main ae2958653d.
